issues.failure_explanation: In computing 2\langle n_{T-t}(Y_t), b(T-t,Y_t)\rangle, the proof replaces 2\langle n,Y\rangle by 2\|n\|^2. Since Y=z+n with z=\Pi_{T-t}(Y), this omits the term 2\langle n,z\rangle. Although n is normal to the ridge at z, z itself need not be orthogonal to its normal space unless the ridge passes through the origin. Hence the displayed equality is false in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the omitted term 2\langle n,z\rangle and bound it by O(\rho R); it is dominated by the existing d\delta^c term for small \delta.
issues.overall_effect: The contraction inequality for D_{T-t}(Y_t) and the normal-error bound in Theorem them:normal contraciton are not established as written.
issues.title: Dropped normal component term in normal contraction proof
issues.why_classification: The missing term is a local correction and does not change the final contraction rate or the qualitative normal-alignment guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the b-approximation term by \|b-...\| \|Y_t-m_{T-t}^{(i)}\|. Lemma lem:application closeness only gives \|b-...\| \le 4R a h^{-1}\theta; it does not imply \|Y_t-m_{T-t}^{(i)}\|=O(R). The center-dominant region B_{T-t}^{(i)} can contain points arbitrarily far along the ridge, so the residual need not be bounded by the data radius. Moreover, the factor h^{-1} in the first inequality is later changed to h^2, so the claimed O(1) bound is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the decay of the softmax error with distance to bound the product \|b-...\|\|Y_t-m_{T-t}^{(i)}\|, or restrict the argument to a bounded tube; also correct the h-power in the displayed inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The tangent contraction inequality and the final tangent-error bound in Theorem them:tangent contraciton are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid bound on approximation error in tangent contraction proof
issues.why_classification: A nontrivial refined estimate or additional bounded-region restriction is needed, but the qualitative tangent-sliding conclusion can plausibly be preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof requires sup_{t\in[\delta,T]} h_t^{1-c}/w(t) \le 1 \vee \delta^{1-c}/w(\delta) (and similarly for the tangent coefficient). For a general decreasing weight such as w(t)=e^{-t}, this fails near t=T, so the stated coefficient is not valid under the stated assumption. It works for power weights like w=1,h_t,h_t^2, but not for arbitrary decreasing w.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace C_\delta^\perp and C_\delta^\parallel by coefficients involving the correct supremum over t, or restrict the theorem to weights satisfying the required decay condition.
issues.overall_effect: The transfer theorem's bounds are not valid for all decreasing weights as claimed; the scope of the theorem is narrower than stated.
issues.title: Transfer coefficient C_delta not valid for general decreasing weights
issues.why_classification: A scope/quantifier error requiring a corrected coefficient or an added weight-class restriction, while the intended power-weight cases remain valid.
